I'm a postdoctoral fellow at [The Ohio State University](https://www.osu.edu/), working with [Dr. Ivy Tso](https://u.osu.edu/ivytsolab/). I received a PhD in Cognitive Psychology from [Rutgers University](https://www.rutgers.edu/) in 2023 (where I have taught courses on [quantitative methods in psychology](https://seredes.github.io/quant-methods-psych/), [cognitive science](https://seredes.github.io/cognitive-lab/), and [expository writing](https://seredes.github.io/exp_writing/)), and I hold a BA in Psychology and Statistics from [Columbia University](https://www.columbia.edu/).

I study how basic perceptual and cognitive processes shape the way we perceive and respond to other people, using behavioral experiments, virtual reality, eye tracking, and computational modeling. [My recent work](about.qmd) examines how people explore faces and interpret eye gaze, and how these processes relate to individual differences in social cognition. My goal is to explain how differences in the way we gather and interpret information contribute to differences in social experience and behavior.
